title: Introduction to Machine Learning Systems
text:
Description
Students study how data pipelines, training, optimization, and deployment work on a single machine with up to eight accelerators. Along the way they build a small deep learning framework, TinyTorch, one module at a time.

title: Introduction to Machine Learning Systems
text:
Learning outcomes
By the end of the course, students can:

Build a small deep learning framework that trains a model.
Measure where time and memory go in a training or inference workload.
Choose optimizations, such as compression, against deployment constraints.
Deploy and evaluate a model against latency, memory, and quality targets.

title: Physical AI
text:
Description
Students build and evaluate a robot whose learned policy proposes each action and whose independent governor decides whether to permit it. Students then measure the resulting motion, and a new observation decides what happens next. The course is a proposed hardware studio and has not yet been taught. These materials are still in preparation for teaching in the next semester or year, so they will change as the course takes shape.

title: Physical AI
text:
Learning outcomes
By the end of the course, students can:

Trace the path from sensing to actuation and name the component that proposes, permits, and executes each action.
Calibrate sensors, measure actuator limits and latency, and set an operating envelope from those measurements.
Compare a simulation with the real hardware and explain where they disagree.
Train a learned policy, deploy it on edge hardware, and compare it with a nonlearned baseline.
Build and test a safety governor, and defend a release decision with evidence from their experiments.

title: Physical AI
text:
Before teaching

The station is a proposal. Before students use it, staff must show the complete command path working on the assembled hardware, including the independent motor cutoff, the operating limits, and restart behavior. Connecting a host directly to the arm’s motor bus does not by itself give the microcontroller authority over each command.
Training needs workstation compute. The course has not fixed a minimum training configuration, policy, simulator, or export path. Staff choose these and measure memory use and run time on the actual equipment. The introductory course’s no-GPU assumption does not apply here.
A trial run comes first. Staff run the full student workflow once before setting enrollment or buying a class set. The trial must show the policy proposing an action, the governor permitting or refusing it, and the arm responding within the measured limits. It also sets station capacity, supervision, and bench time.

The hardware feasibility plan contains the detailed staff preparation. It is a planning document and does not establish that the station has passed qualification.

title: Physical AI
text:

Each offering sets its own dates, deadlines, and policies on late work, collaboration, and AI tools.
An offering can change the task, term length, and hardware once staff qualify the resulting station. The system students build must still separate the policy’s proposals from the governor’s permission.
The ETH Zurich spring 2027 syllabus gives one complete offering, with its labs and assessment.
